arguments.content: # Kutumb Web Frontend Audit Findings Scope: `web/app.js`, `web/index.html`, `web/style.css` — login/signup flow, `api()` fetch helper, auth state, hash routing, XSS, JS correctness. 12 findings. ## CRITICAL 1. **CRITICAL — `web/app.js:125-126` — Tab-switch handlers reference undeclared identifiers `fLogin`/`fSignup`, so clicking either tab throws a ReferenceError and the signup form can never be shown.** Why: the only declarations are the DOM ids `f-login`/`f-signup` (lines 101/106), accessed later via `document.getElementById('f-login')` (line 128); no `const fLogin`/`fSignup` variable exists anywhere in the file (verified by grep), and because the script is a module, undeclared identifiers are unresolvable globals. Trigger: load the default `#/login` route and click "Sign up" — the handler throws before toggling classes, the hidden signup form stays hidden, and signup is completely unreachable through the UI (login still works only because its form is visible by default). ## MEDIUM 2. **MEDIUM — `web/app.js:31-32` — The content-type check `ct.includes('application/json')` misses RFC 7807 `+json` media types (`application/problem+json`, `application/hal+json`, `application/vnd.api+json`), so JSON error bodies under those types are never parsed and users see a bare `HTTP 400/500`.** Why: `includes('application/json')` is substring matching against the raw header; `application/problem+json` does not contain the substring `application/json`. Trigger: the server rejects a signup with `400`, `Content-Type: application/problem+json`, body `{"message":"email already registered"}` — `data` stays `null`, the error becomes generic `HTTP 400`, and the real reason is hidden from the user. 3. **MEDIUM — `web/app.js:32-38` — On a 2xx response with an empty or non-JSON body, `api()` returns `null` instead of an empty object, so callers that immediately read a property (`(await api('/api/login',…)).user`, `t.tree_id`) crash with a TypeError.** Why: `data` is only populated when the content-type includes `application/json`; a `204 No Content` or `200` with `text/plain` leaves it `null`. Trigger: `/api/login` returns 200 with no body — line 132 throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'user')`, caught by the form handler and shown as an opaque banner even though login succeeded. 4. **MEDIUM — `web/app.js:88` / `151` — `/api/me` failures are swallowed (`catch (e) { ME = null; }`), conflating network/server errors with "not authenticated" and silently bouncing logged-in users to the login screen.** Why: a transient 500 or network drop on `/api/me` is indistinguishable from a missing cookie, so `renderTrees` redirects to `#/login` with no banner. Trigger: user is logged in, the server briefly 500s `/api/me`, user refreshes `#/trees` — they land on the login form with no explanation and must log in again. 5. **MEDIUM — `web/app.js:327-330` — `openBigModal` awaits `api('/api/persons/' + pid)` with no try/catch and is invoked from a click handler that doesn't await it, so any request failure leaves the overlay stuck on "Loading person…" forever (unhandled promise rejection).** Why: the loading placeholder at line 329 is only replaced after a successful fetch; on rejection nothing ever clears it, and since `closeOverlay` only runs on explicit close, the modal blocks the UI. Trigger: click a person link for a person id that 404s (or while offline) — the spinner remains indefinitely and the console logs an unhandled rejection. 6. **MEDIUM — `web/app.js:212-213, 222` — Server fields `b.gen` and `c.child_count` are interpolated into `innerHTML` without `esc()`, enabling stored XSS if those values contain HTML.** Why: unlike `t.name`, `c.other_info`, and `couple_id` (which are escaped), `G${b.gen}` and `${c.child_count}` are raw template interpolations. Trigger: an attacker who can influence a couple's `child_count` (e.g. via a tree-edit API) to `1` executes script on every visit to the tree board. 7. **MEDIUM — `web/app.js:47-55` — `splitPartners` returns the same female partner as both `a` and `b` when a couple has no male partner, so an all-female couple renders the same name twice (as "father" and "mother").** Why: with only females, `fa` is `null` and `mo` is the first female; the fallback `if (!mo)` is skipped, and the return `{ a: fa || arr[0], b: mo }` yields `a === b === arr[0]`. Trigger: any couple with two female partners (or a single female partner with `arr[1]` undefined, which instead shows `—` for the second slot) — the father slot shows the mother's name. 8. **MEDIUM — `web/app.js:140-141` — Signup re-uses the signup `FormData` (including `name` and `lang`) for the follow-up `/api/login` call and assumes the response has `.user`, so a signup that succeeds but whose auto-login fails is reported to the user as a failed signup.** Why: `Object.fromEntries(fd)` at line 141 contains `name`, `lang`, `email`, `password`, but the login endpoint may reject unknown fields or return a different shape; the catch at line 143 shows the login error, leaving the user believing the account was not created. Trigger: server requires email verification or rejects extra fields on login — signup returns 201, login returns 400/403, banner shows an error despite the account existing. ## LOW 9. **LOW — `web/app.js:180-186` — Tree creation navigates to `#/tree/${t.tree_id}` with no validation; if the response lacks `tree_id` the hash becomes `#/tree/undefined`, which matches the route regex `/^#\/tree\/([\w-]+)$/` and renders a broken tree page.** Why: `undefined` satisfies `[\w-]+`, so `renderTree('undefined')` fires and calls `/api/trees/undefined/generations` (line 199) instead of the router falling back to `#/login`. Trigger: `/api/trees` POST succeeds but returns a body without `tree_id` (or a proxy strips it) — the user lands on an error banner on a non-existent tree route. 10. **LOW — `web/app.js:265` — The `resize` listener is never removed and fires whenever `GEN_DATA` is set, so resizing the window after leaving the tree view calls `drawWires()` on a removed `#board` and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`.** Why: `drawWires()` does `document.getElementById('board')` and immediately calls `board.querySelector` (lines 237-239); navigating to `#/trees` replaces `app.innerHTML`, destroying `#board` while `GEN_DATA` remains set at module scope. Trigger: view a tree, navigate to the trees list, resize the window — the handler throws on every resize event. 11. **LOW — `web/app.js:72-76` — The router's catch only handles 401; for any other error it shows a banner but leaves the previous screen's DOM in place, so the rendered content can contradict the current hash.** Why: route handlers replace `app.innerHTML` only on success, so a failed `renderTrees` (e.g. `/api/trees` 500) leaves the prior view (possibly the login form) visible while the URL reads `#/trees`. Trigger: `/api/trees` returns 500 after login — banner appears, but the login form (or stale tree list) remains on screen under the trees URL. 12. **LOW — `web/app.js:297-301` — Small-box horizontal positioning mixes document and viewport coordinates and can place the box off-screen when the page is scrolled.** Why: `left` is computed as `r.left + window.scrollX` (document coords) but clamped against `window.innerWidth` (viewport width) without subtracting `scrollX`; the vertical flip check at line 299 handles only the bottom-edge case. Trigger: scroll the page right and click a couple card near the right edge — the box renders clipped/offscreen instead of flipping left.
